Nate: mockups look good, ship the tether
A toast is a 2px band on the top edge of the window it
concerns (purple; rose if critical), drawn by the compositor
and clipped to that window's radius, with the card hanging
8px inside the rect. The band enters from its centre outward;
on timeout the card releases and the band retracts back
toward its centre over 1.4s. No top-right stack, no slide-in.
Rose band with border-pulse breathing (1.2s) while the
state persists. A critical band never retracts on its own.
An app with no visible window hangs its card from the
screen's top edge at its bar entry's x (Spotify's media
chip). Centred if it has no entry. Never over a window
The center is a real tile: the leftmost leaf in tiling, the
left zone in snapping, a column at the left end of the strip
in scrolling. History rows grouped per app with a tabular
age column; a tether ties it back to the bell chip.
Drag a row (or a toast) out of the column: the target rect
lights with a white edge as the pointer crosses it. Drop opens
the app in that rect. Drag off the screen edge dismisses.
